    --name state/rotation-canary --file /tmp/receipt --content-type text/plain --force \
    >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

  sleep 120

  sleep 10

if ! getent hosts hindsight-db >/dev/null 2>&1; then

if [ "$(PGPASSWORD="$(cat /new/password)" psql -h estate-rw.estate-db.svc.cluster.local -U hindsight -d hindsight -tAc "select to_regclass('public.estate_db_migration') is not null")" = t ]; then
  echo "hindsight was copied on an earlier run; leaving it alone"
else
  echo "copying hindsight from hindsight-db into hindsight on the estate cluster"
  PGPASSWORD="$(cat /old/postgres-password)" pg_dump -h hindsight-db -U hindsight -d hindsight \
          --no-owner --no-privileges --exclude-extension=vector --exclude-extension=pg_trgm \
          -Fc -f /tmp/db.dump
  PGPASSWORD="$(cat /new/password)"; export PGPASSWORD
  # Not 'drop schema public cascade' here, which every other Job in this file
  # uses. hindsight's database carries the vector and pg_trgm extensions, both
  # of which live in public, and dropping the schema took them with it: the
  # restore then died on 'type "public.vector" does not exist' (2026-09-04), and
  # the role cannot put vector back because pgvector is not a trusted extension
  # and only a superuser may create it. So drop the application's own objects
  # and leave anything an extension owns where it is.
  psql -h estate-rw.estate-db.svc.cluster.local -U hindsight -d hindsight -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c "
    do \$\$
    declare r record;
    begin
      for r in select c.relname, c.relkind from pg_class c
               join pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.relnamespace
               left join pg_depend d on d.objid = c.oid and d.deptype = 'e'
               where n.nspname = 'public' and d.objid is null
                 and c.relkind in ('r', 'p', 'v', 'm', 'S')
      loop
        execute format('drop %s if exists public.%I cascade',
                       case r.relkind when 'v' then 'view'
                                      when 'm' then 'materialized view'
                                      when 'S' then 'sequence'
                                      else 'table' end, r.relname);
      end loop;
      for r in select p.oid::regprocedure as sig from pg_proc p
               join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace
               left join pg_depend d on d.objid = p.oid and d.deptype = 'e'
               where n.nspname = 'public' and d.objid is null
      loop
        execute format('drop routine if exists %s cascade', r.sig);
      end loop;
      for r in select t.typname from pg_type t
               join pg_namespace n on n.oid = t.typnamespace
               left join pg_depend d on d.objid = t.oid and d.deptype in ('e', 'i')
               where n.nspname = 'public' and d.objid is null
                 and t.typtype in ('e', 'd', 'c')
                 and not exists (select 1 from pg_class c where c.reltype = t.oid)
      loop
        execute format('drop type if exists public.%I cascade', r.typname);
      end loop;
    end
    \$\$;"
  pg_restore -h estate-rw.estate-db.svc.cluster.local -U hindsight -d hindsight --no-owner --no-privileges --exit-on-error /tmp/db.dump
  psql -h estate-rw.estate-db.svc.cluster.local -U hindsight -d hindsight -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 \
       -c 'create table estate_db_migration (copied_at timestamptz not null default now())' \
       -c 'insert into estate_db_migration default values'

  rm -f /tmp/db.dump
  echo "hindsight is on the estate cluster"
fi

# to "" before the pod ever saw it, so the test was always false and gh in
# the live pod reported "not logged into any GitHub hosts" while every
# credential file sat mounted beside it (gate: flux_subst_scan).

  for f in "$HERMES_ENV_DIR"/*; do
    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    n=$(basename "$f")
    case "$n" in [A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*) export "$n=$(cat "$f")" ;; esac

# wrapper for its credential.
printf '#!/bin/sh\nGH_TOKEN=$(cat %s/GITHUB_TOKEN) exec /usr/local/bin/gh "$@"\n' "$HERMES_ENV_DIR" > "$HERMES_HOME/bin/gh"

PGPASSWORD=$(cat "$OTTO_INGRESS_DB_PASSWORD_FILE")
export PGHOST PGPORT PGUSER PGDATABASE PGPASSWORD
# The fork's credentials (GITHUB_TOKEN, EXA key, ESTATE_MCP_KEY ...) arrive as one
# file per name under HERMES_ENV_DIR; export them the way the image's own
# entrypoint does (hermes-v2 deploy/k8s/entrypoint.sh), since this command
# replaces that entrypoint. A missing mount exports nothing and the door
# answers as before, hands empty.
# Only the unbraced form of the variable, never : Flux's
# postBuild substitution reads that as its own default syntax and rewrote it
# to "" before the pod ever saw it, so the test was always false and gh in
# the live pod reported "not logged into any GitHub hosts" while every
# credential file sat mounted beside it (gate: flux_subst_scan).
if [ -d "$HERMES_ENV_DIR" ]; then
  for f in "$HERMES_ENV_DIR"/*; do
    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    n=$(basename "$f")
    case "$n" in [A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*) export "$n=$(cat "$f")" ;; esac
  done
fi
mkdir -p "$HERMES_HOME/skills" "$HERMES_HOME/bin"
# The image's skills (82 SKILL.md under /app/hermes-agent/skills on main-92) never
# reached HERMES_HOME because this command replaces the image entrypoint: the
# door answered "skills_list: 0" on 2026-09-06 while they sat one directory over.
# No clobber, so a skill edited on the volume survives an image update.
cp -Rn /app/hermes-agent/skills/. "$HERMES_HOME/skills/" 2>/dev/null || true
# gh in the model's shell. hermes-agent's terminal tool strips GH_TOKEN and
# GITHUB_TOKEN from the environment it hands the model (tools/environments/
# local.py), so the token exported above never reaches gh, and the live pod
# answered "You are not logged into any GitHub hosts" (2026-09-06, the
# "unverified" Telegram replies). The token is the one-hour installation token
# the GithubAccessToken generator mints (agent-env.yaml), so a one-time
# `gh auth login` would go stale within the hour; this wrapper reads the
# mounted file, which kubelet refreshes, on every call. Git borrows the same
# wrapper for its credential.
printf '#!/bin/sh\nGH_TOKEN=$(cat %s/GITHUB_TOKEN) exec /usr/local/bin/gh "$@"\n' "$HERMES_ENV_DIR" > "$HERMES_HOME/bin/gh"
chmod 0755 "$HERMES_HOME/bin/gh"
PATH="$HERMES_HOME/bin:$PATH"
export PATH
git config --global credential.helper "!$HERMES_HOME/bin/gh auth git-credential"
git config --global --add safe.directory '*'
exec python -m otto.ingress

args:
set -eu
# Both credentials arrive as FILES and are exported here. The estate's
# admission policy refuses a workload that takes a secret from an env var,
# and the engine reads its configuration from the environment, so this line
# is the join between the two.
LITELLM_API_KEY="$(cat /secrets/router/LITELLM_API_KEY)"
# The estate's one Postgres, one database on it, not a server of our own.
# The database and the role are declared to the operator in
# platform/estate-db/cluster/databases.yaml, so nothing here creates either.
PG="postgresql://research:$(cat /secrets/db/POSTGRES_PASSWORD)@estate-rw.estate-db.svc.cluster.local:5432"
RESEARCH_PG_DSN="${PG}/research"
export LITELLM_API_KEY RESEARCH_PG_DSN
# One line per hour, rotating through the intake without a scheduler
# holding state. Each line is `lane: subject`: the lane names a profile
# in the engine, and the profile holds the questions it asks (SPEC-v1 §8),
# so changing what a lane asks is a change in the engine's repository and
# changing what it asks about is a change here.
n=$(grep -c . /questions/subjects)
i=$(( ($(date -u +%H) % n) + 1 ))
line=$(sed -n "${i}p" /questions/subjects)
lane=${line%%:*}
subject=${line#*: }
echo "research-engine running lane ${lane} on subject ${i} of ${n}"
exec python -m engine.cli run --profile "$lane" --subject "$subject" --out /state

args:
set -eu
# temporal-db. If it is not there at all there is nothing to copy, and this Job
# is finished rather than failed -- see the note at the top of this file.
i=0
while [ $i -lt 12 ]; do
  getent hosts temporal-db >/dev/null 2>&1 && break
  i=$((i + 1))
  sleep 10
done
if ! getent hosts temporal-db >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "temporal-db does not resolve; there is no old server to empty"
  exit 0
fi
if [ "$(PGPASSWORD="$(cat /new/password)" psql -h estate-rw.estate-db.svc.cluster.local -U temporal -d temporal -tAc "select to_regclass('public.estate_db_migration') is not null")" = t ]; then
  echo "temporal was copied on an earlier run; leaving it alone"
else
  echo "copying temporal from temporal-db into temporal on the estate cluster"
  PGPASSWORD="$(cat /old/password)" pg_dump -h temporal-db -U temporal -d temporal \
          --no-owner --no-privileges --exclude-extension=vector --exclude-extension=pg_trgm \
          -Fc -f /tmp/db.dump
  PGPASSWORD="$(cat /new/password)"; export PGPASSWORD
  psql -h estate-rw.estate-db.svc.cluster.local -U temporal -d temporal -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 \
       -c 'drop schema if exists public cascade' -c 'create schema public'
  pg_restore -h estate-rw.estate-db.svc.cluster.local -U temporal -d temporal --no-owner --no-privileges --exit-on-error /tmp/db.dump
  psql -h estate-rw.estate-db.svc.cluster.local -U temporal -d temporal -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 \
       -c 'create table estate_db_migration (copied_at timestamptz not null default now())' \
       -c 'insert into estate_db_migration default values'
  unset PGPASSWORD
  rm -f /tmp/db.dump
  echo "temporal is on the estate cluster"
fi
if [ "$(PGPASSWORD="$(cat /new/password)" psql -h estate-rw.estate-db.svc.cluster.local -U temporal -d temporal_visibility -tAc "select to_regclass('public.estate_db_migration') is not null")" = t ]; then
